title: Effect of low‐dose proton pump inhibitor on preventing upper gastrointestinal bleeding in chronic kidney disease patients receiving aspirin

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:title>Background and Aim</jats:title><jats:p>Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">UGIB</jats:styled-content>) leads to significant morbidity and mortality in chronic kidney disease (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CKD</jats:styled-content>) patients. This study determined the efficacy of using a low‐dose proton pump inhibitor (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content>) to reduce the risk of non‐variceal <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">UGIB</jats:styled-content> in <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CKD</jats:styled-content> patients receiving aspirin.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods</jats:title><jats:p>We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of 500 <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CKD</jats:styled-content> patients who received aspirin between <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">J</jats:styled-content>anuary 2008 and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">M</jats:styled-content>arch 2013. Cumulative incidence analysis using the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">K</jats:styled-content>aplan–<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">M</jats:styled-content>eier method was performed to analyze the rate of non‐variceal <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">UGIB</jats:styled-content> and association with the administration of low‐dose <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content>.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>Of the 500 patients, 191 received low‐dose <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content>. Over the follow‐up period, which lasted 1067 person‐years, three patients in the low‐dose <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content> group (8.9 per 1000 person‐years) and 19 patients in the non‐<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content> group (25.9 per 1000 person‐years) developed non‐variceal <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">UGIB</jats:styled-content>, respectively (<jats:italic>P</jats:italic> = 0.113). Low‐dose <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content> use did not decrease the risk of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">UGIB</jats:styled-content> in <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CKD</jats:styled-content> patients, including patients who did not receive dialysis (<jats:italic>P</jats:italic> = 0.127). However, according to the subgroup analysis of 230 patients who received dialysis, the low‐dose <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content> group (14.4 per 1000 person‐years) demonstrated significantly reduced incidence and risk of non‐variceal <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">UGIB</jats:styled-content> in comparison with the non‐<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content> group (53.8 per 1000 person‐years) (<jats:italic>P</jats:italic> = 0.032).</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title><jats:p>Prophylactic low‐dose <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content> can reduce the risk of non‐variceal <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">UGIB</jats:styled-content> in dialysis patients receiving aspirin.</jats:p></jats:sec>
